newsitem.title: UK: Formula One stock float on track again - report.
newsitem.headline: Formula One stock float on track again - report.

text.p: Formula One Grand Prix motor racing could now float on the stock exchange ahead of the Silverstone Grand Prix in July, Britain's Sunday Times newspaper reported.
The plans, first reported in March as targeted for the middle of the year, were said at the beginning of May to have been postponed.
Newspaper reports said then that there were also queries over a 2.5 billion pounds ($4.1 billion) price tag put on Formula One's business.

The Sunday Times said that Salomon Brothers, the investment bank handling the flotation, had told City backers last week that final arrangements were being settled with an announcement possible this week.
The newspaper said that Formula One's multi-millionaire owner Bernie Ecclestone had been persuaded to cut his stake to about 30 percent with some 50 percent of the business to be floated.
It added that Helmut Werner, former head of Mercedes-Benz, had been targeted as chairman for the new company.
The Sunday Times said that Salomon gave forecasts of 200 million pounds for turnover this year with pretax profits of 85 million pounds. ($1 = 0.611 British Pounds)
